1.note: Amos is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [It was significant that]

The phrase **after the mowings of the king** means that the king had the right to take the first cutting of hay from the fields for his own use, so the crop that the locusts were about to eat was all that was left for the people to use for themselves and their animals. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [after the king’s men had cut the first hay for him, so it was the crop the people needed for themselves and their animals]

2.note: The pronoun **it** refers to the locust swarm mentioned in the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the locust swarm had finished]

Amos is using the question form for emphasis, to express his conviction that the people of Jacob will not be able to survive such a disaster. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Jacob will surely not be able to stand!]

Here, Amos is using the name **Jacob** to refer to the people of Israel who were all descendants of the patriarch Jacob, who was also known as Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the nation of Israel]

Amos is speaking of Jacob as if he were physically **small**. He means that the people of Jacob are weak and would be unable to survive this locust plague. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he is weak]

3.note: The pronoun **this** refers to the destruction by locusts that Yahweh had shown Amos in the vision. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh relented concerning this locust plague]

4.note: Amos is speaking of the fire as if it were a creature that **devoured** the waters and the land. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And it destroyed the great deep and was destroying the portion]
By **the great deep**, Amos means the ocean. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the ocean]

The implication is that **the portion** is the land that Yahweh had assigned to the Israelites as their own share. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the land Yahweh had allotted to his people]

5.q: מִ֥י יָק֖וּם יַעֲקֹ֑ב כִּ֥י קָטֹ֖ן הֽוּא
5.note: See how you translated these same phrases in verse 2.

6.note: The pronoun **this** refers to the destruction by fire that Yahweh had shown Amos in the vision. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh relented concerning this judgment by fire]

7.note: Here, **the Lord was standing beside a wall of a plumb line** represents Yahweh coming to examine his people to see whether they measure up to his standard, just as a builder examines a wall to see whether it is straight. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could include this information in a footnote. Alternate translation: [the Lord was standing beside a wall to inspect it, ready to test his people against his standard]
The word translated as **plumb line** could mean: (1) a plumb line, as in the ULT and UST or (2) a type of metal called “tin.” Alternate translation: [a tin wall and in his hand was tin]

Amos is using the possessive form to describe a **wall** that is characterized by being made perfectly straight by using **a plumb line**, a builder’s tool made of a string with a heavy weight at the end that hangs straight down, used to check if a wall or structure is completely vertical. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a wall that had been made straight by using a plumb line]

8.q: עַמִּ֣⁠י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹֽא־אוֹסִ֥יף ע֖וֹד עֲב֥וֹר לֽ⁠וֹ
8.note: In this verse, the word **him** is singular in form, but it refers to all of the Israelites as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “him.” Alternate translation: [my people Israel. I will not again repeat to pass over them]
As in verse 7, also in this verse the word translated as **plumb line** could mean: (1) a plumb line, as in the ULT and UST or (2) a type of metal called “tin.” Alternate translation: [Tin … tin]

8.q: הִנְ⁠נִ֨י שָׂ֤ם אֲנָךְ֙ בְּ⁠קֶ֨רֶב֙ עַמִּ֣⁠י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
8.note: Yahweh holding **a plumb line** was a symbolic action by which he showed that he was going to measure his people’s behavior. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [Behold me setting a standard by which I will measure my people Israel]

Yahweh is using **Behold me** as a common expression of the culture to mean that he is about to do something. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am about to place]

Yahweh is using **pass over** as a common expression of the culture to mean “overlook their sin.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will no longer forgive their sins]

9.q: וְ⁠נָשַׁ֨מּוּ֙ בָּמ֣וֹת יִשְׂחָ֔ק וּ⁠מִקְדְּשֵׁ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יֶחֱרָ֑בוּ
9.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [And all the worship places of the Israelites will surely be left in ruins]

The expression **will be deserted** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And I will destroy the high places of Isaac so they will be deserted]

Here, **the high places** represent the shrines that the Israelites built on hilltops for worshiping idols. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the idolatrous places where the Israelites worshiped]

Here, **Isaac** represents all the people of Israel, as they were all descended from Isaac. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the Israelites]

Here Yahweh is speaking of sending enemies to fight against them as if he would physically **rise**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will attack]

Here, **the house of Jeroboam** represents “the royal family descended from Jeroboam.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the royal line of those descended from Jeroboam]
Here, **the sword** represents “warfare.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [with warfare]

10.q: וַ⁠יִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֲמַצְיָה֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל אֶל־יָרָבְעָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל
10.note: Amos is introducing **Amaziah, the priest of Bethel** as a new participant in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation.

Amos is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Then Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent a message to Jeroboam]

Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **the house of Israel** figuratively means all the people descended from the patriarch Jacob, who was also known as Israel. Alternate translation: [the Israelites]

Amaziah says **The land is not able to contain all of his words** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [The people of this land cannot endure everything he is saying]

11.q: כִּי־כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר עָמ֔וֹס בַּ⁠חֶ֖רֶב יָמ֣וּת יָרָבְעָ֑ם
11.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [For Amos says that Jeroboam will die by the sword]

Here, **the sword** represents violent death in battle. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Jeroboam will die violently in battle]
Here, **Israel** represents the nation of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and the Israelites]

Amos is repeating forms of the verb **go into exile** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [will certainly be taken far away into exile]

12.note: Amaziah is using **eat bread there** as a common expression of the culture to mean to earn what one needs to be able to eat. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and make your living there]

Even though Amos has been speaking of himself in the first person as “I” and “me”, here he switches to speaking of himself in the third person as **Amos** to recount the exchange with Amaziah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person for consistency. Alternate translation: [And Amaziah said to me]

13.q: וּ⁠בֵֽית־אֵ֔ל לֹֽא־תוֹסִ֥יף ע֖וֹד לְ⁠הִנָּבֵ֑א כִּ֤י מִקְדַּשׁ־מֶ֨לֶךְ֙ ה֔וּא וּ⁠בֵ֥ית מַמְלָכָ֖ה הֽוּא
13.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [But because it is a sanctuary of the king and it is a house of a kingdom, at Bethel you shall not repeat to prophesy again]

Amaziah is using **you shall not repeat to prophesy again** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you must not prophesy any more.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you must never prophesy any more]

The implication is that by using the phrase**a house of a kingdom** which implies a royal temple, Amaziah is claiming that Bethel is a temple of the northern kingdom of Israel. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and it is the royal temple of the northern kingdom of Israel]

14.note: As in verse 12, Amos is speaking of himself in the third person as **Amos**. If you chose to translate it in the first person there, you should do so here as well. Alternate translation: [And I answered and said to Amaziah]

The terms **answered and said** together introduce a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent both terms explicitly as modeled in the UST.

14.q: לֹא־נָבִ֣יא אָנֹ֔כִי וְ⁠לֹ֥א בֶן־נָבִ֖יא אָנֹ֑כִי כִּֽי־בוֹקֵ֥ר אָנֹ֖כִי
14.note: Since this verse has no verbs in the original, this could mean: (1) that Amos is not currently a professional prophet or part of a group of prophets but a herdsman, as modeled in the UST and UST or (2) that Amos was a herdsman and not a prophet before Yahweh called him to prophesy. Alternate translation: [I was not a prophet, and I was not a son of a prophet, for I was a herdsman]

Amos is using **a son of a prophet** as a common expression of the culture to mean “a disciple of a prophet.” He is making a point that he did not make his living as a prophet as those who were considered part of the official group of prophets did. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly as modeled in the UST.

The term **sycamore figs** describes a kind of fruit that grows on a large tree that was common in the warm, low-lying areas of that region. If your readers would not be familiar with what sycamore figs are, you could use the name of a similar fruit that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a kind of fig]

15.note: Amos is using **took me from after the flock** as a common expression of the culture to mean “took me away from tending sheep.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [But Yahweh took me away from my work of caring for the sheep]

15.q: וַ⁠יֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַ⁠י֙ יְהוָ֔ה לֵ֥ךְ הִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל־עַמִּ֥⁠י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
15.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh told me to go prophesy to his people Israel]

16.note: Here, **the word of Yahweh** represents the message that Yahweh is speaking through Amos. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the message that Yahweh has for me to give you]

Amaziah is speaking of prophesying or preaching as if it were words that **drip** from the prophet’s mouth, letting words fall like rain. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you shall not preach]

Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **the house of Isaac** means all the people descended from the patriarch Isaac which is all the people of Israel. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]

17.note: The implication is that enemy soldiers will capture the city and force Amaziah’s wife to become a prostitute. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Your wife will be forced to become a prostitute in the city when enemy soldiers capture it]

The expression **will be divided** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and enemies will divide your ground with the measuring line]

Here, **the measuring line** represents “the parceling out of land to new owners,” since people used such a line to mark off the boundaries of property. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [into parcels for new owners]

The implication is that **unclean ground** is a foreign land where people worship other gods, so that it is not a fit place for a worshiper of Yahweh to live. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and you, you will die in a foreign land that is defiled by the worship of other gods]

Amos is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you will die** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is now address Amaziah’s own fate. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [and you, yourself will die]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:11.
